title: What do you think of 2010s films? What are your favourite films from that decade?

commenti.body: I agree that superhero movies are lame in general, but there were some really great films released in the 2010s. Some of my favorites are Dunkirk, The Grand Budapest Hotel, Inside Llewyn Davis, The Irishman, It Follows, Lincoln, Mad Max: Fury Road, Once Upon a Time... in Hollywood, Silence, The Social Network, Uncut Gems, Under the Skin, The Witch, and Zero Dark Thirty.

*First Man* is definitely a very well-made and satisfying movie, even if I think it just misses out on being a truly great film. 


My favorites from the 2010s so far --- and the only two I consider true masterpieces from that decade --- are *The Master* and *The Lighthouse*. 


I say this, of course, with the disclaimer that I still need to catch up on a fairly decent-sized backlog of movies from that decade; I'm sure there are other greats I haven't seen yet.
The Master was very good. That was a cool film.

Oh yeah, I forgot about Hanna. Really enjoyed that one. I think it's not really fair to dismiss a whole decade, especially since quite a few of my all-time favorites are from 2010-2020. Here's a random list of films made in the 2010's that any self-respecting cinephile needs to see if they haven't already:

Holy Motors, Long Day's Journey into Night (2018), Under The Skin, Border, The Endless, The Invitation, Coherence, Blue Ruin, Green Room, Inherent Vice, It Follows, Under The Silver Lake, The Myth of the American Sleepover, Blade Runner 2049, Prisoners, Enemy, Sicario, Drive, Only God Forgives, Kill List, Spring Breakers, Arrival, Swiss Army Man, The Florida Project, The Vast of Night, The Lobster, The Favouite, Thoroghbreds, Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Knives Out....


I mean, come on.

For a while towards the end of that decade I had a yearly membership to a fantastic cinema that showed films that catered extremely well to local educated tastes. Among the great films that were shown were:

The Tree of Life (2011): Terence Malick's unique cinematic vision with a distinctly theological element. Often regarded as one of the great films of the decade.

Happy as Lazzaro (2018): An Italian neo-realist influenced film with magical realism elements that tackles issues of class, oppression, and innocence.

Foxtrot (2017): An Israeli film that tackles the moral problems, grief and struggles associated with being part of the armed forces in a country in constant conflict.

First Cow (2019): Another film that looks at the issue of class. Quiet, funny and with marvelous cinematography.

Nightcrawler (2014): A terrifying look at how the structure of modern Western Society both leads to the rise of concienceless exploiters, the moral degeneration of those desperate to be successful at any cost, and how the media is at the centre of such issues.

Searching (2018): A pioneering film that shows only what appears on computer screens. A drama about a missing girl whose father searches for her.

Phantom Thread (2017): A peculiar and surprising romance between a dressmaker and a woman.

The Wild Pear Tree (2018): A slow Turkish masterpiece, criminally underseen, about a young aspiring novelist.

Marriage Story (2019): A touching, sometimes funny film about a couple trying to amicably divorce.

And so many others. It was a fine decade if your viewing was well curated.
